# What goes here

A spec is a proposed change: what it is for, what was decided, and the order of work. `docs/specs/` holds the specs
being written or in progress, and `docs/done/` the closed ones. Open problems go in `docs/backlog/`, and what was
done in `docs/log.md`. Start from [index.md](index.md).

# One spec

One spec is one file, `docs/specs/<slug>.md`. The slug never changes once the file exists, because commit messages,
other documents and the `epic` of other specs refer to it. The frontmatter holds the fields used for filtering.
Everything else goes in the body.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Spec` |
| `title` | Display name |
| `description` | One sentence: what the spec changes |
| `tags` | Exactly one area, one of the `areas` declared in `.config/rotproof.toml`. The index groups specs by it, in that order |
| `status` | `draft` (not agreed yet), `stable` (agreed) or `deprecated` (closed) |
| `epic` | Optional. The slug of the spec this one is a part of. See "Epics" |

The body is free, except that a closed spec has `# Resolution`.

# Directories

The directory answers only "current or finished"; the status says the rest.

| Directory | Status |
|---|---|
| `docs/specs/` | `draft` or `stable` |
| `docs/done/` | `deprecated` |

- **A spec describes the current state.** When it disagrees with the implementation, fix it in the same commit. A
  rejected design left looking current is read as correct by the next reader.
- **Closing moves the file to `docs/done/`.** Set `status: deprecated` and write `# Resolution`: implemented or
  dropped, and how the implementation differs from the spec. From then on it is history. The slug stays the same, and
  a slug is in one of the two directories, never both.
- **Links between documents are markdown links.** `docs/specs/` and `docs/done/` sit at the same depth, so a relative
  link inside a spec survives the move.

# Areas

An area says where a spec belongs, and never closes. A spec that cannot name one area mixes two: split it into one
spec per area, and tie them back together as parts of an epic.

# Epics

An epic says which piece of work a spec is part of, and closes when the work is finished. It is not a document type
of its own: a spec that other specs name in `epic` is an epic, and keeps its own goals, decisions and order of work.

- **A part names its epic by slug,** not by path, so the relation survives the epic's move to `docs/done/`. The slug
  names a spec in `docs/specs/` or `docs/done/`: a backlog item or a guide is not a spec, and a spec is not its own
  epic.
- **One level only.** An epic has no `epic` of its own.
- **A part may be in another area than its epic.** The area and the epic are independent.
- **An epic closes after its parts.** An epic in `docs/done/` has no part in `docs/specs/`. A part that is dropped
  instead closes as dropped, as any spec does. A draft part that turns out to be work of its own removes its `epic`.
- **A spec written after its epic closed is not a part of it.** The work it belonged to is finished: the new spec
  starts a new epic or stands alone, and the area connects it to the earlier work.

In an index, a part in the same area and the same directory as its epic is listed under it, indented. Any other part
is listed under its own area with `Epic: [<title>](...)` after its line.

# Index

[index.md](index.md) is generated. After adding, changing or moving a spec, run `rotproof index`. `rotproof check` fails
when the index differs from what `rotproof index` writes.

# Differences from OKF

- `epic` is an extension field, which OKF allows. OKF expresses relations between documents with links and the prose
  around them; `epic` is a field so that Rotproof can check it. The index writes it as a link.
